reason: The cited evidence supports that serrated flow in HEAs is linked to solute pinning (E1, E2) and occurs in a specific temperature/strain-rate window (E1, E3), but no evidence compares Co-free vs. Co-containing alloys or supports the claim that the Co-free variant will show more pronounced serrations; the baseline comparison and acoustic emission premise are unsupported.
premises: Serrated flow in HEAs arises from dislocation pinning by solute atoms (DSA/PLC mechanism).
Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit more pronounced DSA serrations than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
DSA serration intensity peaks in an intermediate temperature/strain-rate window.
Acoustic emission can monitor dislocation dynamics and serration events.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy shows less pronounced DSA under similar conditions.
